messages:
owen: Heads-up: spotted a weirdness on latency dashboard for /v2/embeds — p95 briefly drops below p50 around 11:10UTC. screenshot: https://redwood.internal/dash/shot555 :thinking:
priya: That usually means the series are coming from different derivations (tdigest vs hist rollup) or different scopes (region vs global). Can you paste the panel queries?
owen: Panel uses 3 series: p50 from a global rollup median, p95 from regional tdigest p95, p99 from a merged-rollup quantile. gist: 
```
# p50 (global rollup median)
SELECT median(lat_ms) FROM rollup_hist WHERE endpoint='/v2/embeds' GROUP BY time(1m)
# p95 (region tdigest)
SELECT quantile(0.95)(lat_ms) FROM tdigest('tq') WHERE region='us-east1' AND endpoint='/v2/embeds' GROUP BY time(1m)
```
kyle: Oh yea mixing median vs quantiles + cross-region vs region-specific scope will produce non-monotonic plots. UX should never plot mixed-derivation percentiles on same axis without explicit provenance.
priya: For a quick fix, switch p50 to region tdigest median. Also overlay sample_count. Low N will still produce noisy quantiles.
ui-bot: created ticket UI-4987 "percentile derivation badge + legend detail" by priya :memo:
infra-bot: INFRA-3357 flagged: rollups currently store histograms; proposal to store tdigest summaries for reconstructible quantiles. 17 panels affected.
owen: I pushed a patch to point p50 -> region tdigest median. deploy-bot: dashboard deploy by owen started at 11:24UTC :rocket:
priya: After switch the chart looks monotonic again. p50 <= p95 <= p99. We should add a dashboard linter to detect mixed-derivation series and a monitor that alerts when p50>p95 for same endpoint+time.
kyle: I'll own the linter change. It will scan panel queries and flag differing sources (tdigest|hist|rollup_quantiles) per percentile metric.
priya: Also add a small confidence band based on sample_count and show sample_count as faint bar under the chart. That helps teams interpret noisy inversions.
owen: Filed follow-ups: INFRA-3357 (tdigest rollup), UI-4987 (legend/provenance), and MON-1202 (monotonicity alert). Closing this thread unless infra finds additional root causes. Thanks! :white_check_mark:
